subject.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction

question: Should default `openclaw doctor --lint` intentionally become warning-failing for existing configurations that set a positive byte guard without enabling transcript truncation?
rationale: The change is diagnostically useful but can alter existing lint automation and operator workflows even though it does not alter compaction runtime behavior.

options.title: Accept the default warning
options.body: Keep the check enabled by default and document that existing inactive byte-guard configurations now produce a warning and nonzero lint outcome.

options.title: Make the diagnostic opt-in
options.body: Retain the check but require an explicit Doctor selection if maintainers do not want existing lint automation to change.

recommendation.title: Accept the default warning
recommendation.body: Keep the check enabled by default and document that existing inactive byte-guard configurations now produce a warning and nonzero lint outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor can provide the requested CLI proof and clarify the intended operator-facing behavior, while repository owners should make the final compatibility decision.
